prompt:
A Click parameter has three strings for three audiences: `decls` (what the developer passes to the decorator), `spec` (what the user reads in --help and types on the command line) and `name` (the internal Python name). Click has no attribute for the spec: Parameter.human_readable_name returns the internal name for options, so messages say `The option 'my_option' is deprecated.` where the user typed `--my-option`. Introduce `spec`, use it everywhere Click shows a parameter to the user, and deprecate human_readable_name.

Changelog entries for this change:
- Add Parameter.spec, which returns how the user spells the parameter on the command line: `--times` for an option declared as `-t`, `--times`, and `FILENAME` for an argument declared as `filename`.
- Move get_help_spec from Option to Parameter, and give Argument an override that returns its metavar.
- Error messages and deprecation warnings name an option by its spec instead of its internal name, so they read `The option '--my-option' is deprecated.` where they read `The option 'my_option' is deprecated.` before.
- Parameter.human_readable_name is deprecated and will be removed in Click 9.0. Use Parameter.spec instead. It returned the internal name for options, so its value changes from `my_option` to `--my-option`. Click no longer reads it, and a subclass that overrides it gets a warning when the class is defined.

For `@click.argument('recipe')` and `@click.option('-g', '--gluten-free/--no-gluten-free')`: spec is `RECIPE` and `--gluten-free`; name is `recipe` and `gluten_free`; opts are `['recipe']` and `['-g', '--gluten-free']`.

API (docstrings):
- `Parameter.spec` (property): "Returns how the user spells this parameter on the command line. This is the declaration with the longest prefix, so an option declared as "-t", "--times" returns --times. Click derives name from that same declaration, unless the developer passed an explicit name. A parameter without declarations returns its name."
- `Argument.spec` (property): "Returns the argument's metavar, which is how the user reads it in --help. An argument has no flag to spell, so this is the metavar if one was given, and the uppercased name otherwise."
- `Parameter.get_help_spec(ctx)`: "Returns the left column of this parameter's help record. This implementation returns spec. Option returns every spelling, plus the metavar when the option takes a value. Argument returns its metavar, which already carries the markers for an optional, repeated or deprecated value. Unlike get_help_record(), the spec is produced even when the parameter is left out of the help page, like a hidden option."
- `Argument.get_help_spec(ctx)`: "Returns the left column of the argument's help record: its metavar, like FILENAME or [FILENAME]." An argument's help record (get_help_record) uses it as its left column.
- `Parameter.human_readable_name` (deprecated property): returns spec and emits DeprecationWarning "'human_readable_name' is deprecated and will be removed in Click 9.0. Use 'spec' instead."
- Defining a subclass of Parameter (or Option, Argument) that overrides human_readable_name emits, at class definition, DeprecationWarning "<ClassName> overrides 'human_readable_name'. Click no longer reads that property. Override 'spec' instead. Click will remove 'human_readable_name' in 9.0." A subclass that does not override it emits nothing.

## Contract (also checked)
- Option spec examples: ["-t", "--times"] and ["--times", "-t"] give --times; ["-t"] gives -t; ["-t", "--times", "--repeat"] gives --times; ["--color/--no-color"] gives --color; ["/debug;/no-debug"] gives /debug; ["--times", "repeat_count"] (explicit name) gives --times with name repeat_count. The name is still derived from that same declaration.
- Argument examples: Argument(["filename"]) spec FILENAME, help spec FILENAME; required=False: help spec [FILENAME]; nargs=-1: [FILENAME]...; metavar="<file>": spec and help spec <file>.
- Everything Click shows to the user (error messages, deprecation warnings, hints) uses spec where it used human_readable_name; Click itself never reads human_readable_name.
